title: fix(cli)!: os migrate apply --allow-destructive holds back every organization_id drop until the organization-ownership ceremony verifies (#23684)
body:
Fixes #23684
Clause-②: no (narrowing)

## What changed

`os migrate apply --allow-destructive` now holds back every `organization_id` drop that the schema-drift report offers, until the organization-ownership ceremony's marker is verified. The marker is the `sys_migration` row `adr-0131-organization-ownership`.

- **The gate** is `packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-drop-gate.ts`. It held back only the tables in the platform inventory (`CEREMONY_TABLES`), so an `organization_id` drop on a host-declared platform-global object (ADR-0131 D7) was applied ahead of the ceremony. Now the gate holds back every one.
- **Its header** now states which tables are covered and why.
- **`apply.ts` is unchanged.** The call site and its refusal are reused as they are: the text, the `--json` envelope `refused_organization_ownership_unmigrated`, exit 1, and the hold on the whole run.
- **No new flag, no `packages/spec` change, and no second copy of the ceremony's inventory composition.**

The contract text that already states this refusal:

- The gate's header: the drop "waits for the ceremony's verified marker … ⛔ No flag stands it down".
- ADR-0131 D10 item 5: a v18 runtime refuses to boot against a database the ceremony has not completed, with "no escape hatch that silently skips the check".

## Hypothesis (a): every `organization_id` drop is the ceremony's table set (measured, holds)

- **The ceremony's plan meets every physical base table that carries `organization_id`.** The table loop is in `organization-ownership-plan.ts`, from `:1146` on `c9810dd9d`. Each such table gets one of four answers:
  - its inventory row;
  - its `--fate-supplement` row;
  - `APPLICATION_OBJECT_FATE`, for any other table;
  - the `uninventoried-platform-table` refusal, for a platform-prefixed table with no row.

  A table without the column is counted in `outsideCeremony` and skipped.
- **The drift can offer to drop only a column that is physically there.** So on the primary database, every `organization_id` drop it proposes is on a table the ceremony plans. There, no v18 drift proposes an `organization_id` drop on a table the ceremony does not own, whether an app object or a cloud object (cloud objects are inventory placeholder rows or supplement rows). On the primary database, the rule does not over-refuse.
- **The ceremony drops a column only through the drift.** `dropColumnsThroughDrift` in `organization-ownership-column-drops.ts` (`:38`) keeps only the `drop_column` entries the drift proposed. So every `organization_id` drop the ceremony could ever perform is one this rule holds back. That includes a fate-supplement object, which `apply` cannot read.
- **The v18 boot refusal judges the same population.** `findV17ShapeTables` (`packages/runtime/src/organization-ownership-boot-guard.ts:139`) checks every registered object with `systemFields.tenant: false` and no declared `organization_id` whose table still carries the column; the inventory plays no part. A drop ahead of the marker on any of those tables hides the table from that refusal. That is the escape hatch D10 item 5 forbids.
- **Where the rule is stricter than the inventory and the declarations:**
  - An application object that authors `systemFields: { tenant: false }` over a table that still carries the column. The ceremony plans that table with the application-object fate, and the boot refusal refuses over it too.
  - The `telemetry` sibling datasource. `apply` reconciles it, but the ceremony's plan does not read it.
- **Corpus reading on `c9810dd9d`.** The tenant opt-out pattern (a `tenant` value of false, or `systemFields` set to false) has 0 hits in `examples/**/*.ts`, which holds 26 object files. The control is the same pattern over `packages/**/*.object.ts`: 14 files. So no example app object is held by the stricter half.

## Hypothesis (b): the composed set is not built

The composed set would be the inventory plus the `org-scoping` declaration, read at the call site. It would not cover the fate supplement:

- The supplement is a flag of the ceremony (`--fate-supplement FILE`), and `apply` never sees it.
- A supplement object whose own metadata opts out of the column, rather than the deployment's declaration, has no other reading at `apply`.
- Covering it would need a new `apply` flag.

Rule (a) covers such an object with no flag: the drift offers its drop exactly when the ceremony itself could drop it. So (b) is not needed, and this PR returns no `needs_decision`.

## Hypothesis (c): the existing fixture

The pins extend PR #23681's fixture file in place (`packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-platform-global-column-drop.integration.test.ts`), with no new rig. They reuse its host composition and its v17 template database:

- the host's own lazy engine;
- an `org-scoping` provider that declares `sys_osgc_ledger` and `sys_osgc_held` platform-global;
- three host objects.

The new `describe` block runs the real `os migrate apply --allow-destructive --yes --json` three times:

1. With no marker: refused, naming the ceremony, and nothing is dropped.
2. CONTROL: with a verified marker, the drop applies.
3. CONTROL: a destructive drop of another column is unchanged.

## Before / after (fixture; table × marker state)

| column | marker | before (base `c9810dd9d`) | after (this PR) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sys_osgc_ledger.organization_id` (host-declared platform-global) | absent | **applied**, exit 0 | **held**, exit 1, `refused_organization_ownership_unmigrated` |
| `sys_osgc_held.organization_id` (host-declared platform-global) | absent | **applied**, exit 0 | **held** (same refusal; `tables: [sys_osgc_held, sys_osgc_ledger]`) |
| both of the above | verified | applied | applied |
| `sys_osgc_audit.organization_id` (not declared) | any | not proposed, kept | not proposed, kept |
| `sys_osgc_ledger.legacy_23684_note` (another column; no `organization_id` drop in the run) | absent | applied | applied |
| `sys_platform_setting.organization_id` (platform inventory; existing pins) | absent or unverified | held | held |
| `sys_platform_setting.organization_id` | verified | applied | applied |

## Tests

The tests ran on `cf15feedf4`. The head `9b3d9d8daf` adds only the changeset file on top of it.

- **Red leg** (base `c9810dd9d` plus the pin, fix absent): `Tests 1 failed | 2 passed | 3 skipped (6)`, with `AssertionError: {"appliedOrganizationDrops":["sys_osgc_held","sys_osgc_ledger"]}: expected +0 to be 1`. The two controls were green.
- **Green leg**: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --project integration --maxWorkers=2` over the fixture file and `src/commands/migrate/apply-organization-ownership-gate.integration.test.ts` gave `Test Files 2 passed (2)`, `Tests 11 passed (11)`.
- **Ablation**: `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` put the table set back to the platform inventory only, with a restore trap.
  - On-disk proof: anchor x1 to x0, replacement x0 to x1, blob `8d8ebfc14096` to `bea1fc2829b0`, marker `grep -c` 0 / 1 / 0.
  - Result: the first pin went red with the same message, while the 2 new controls and the 5 existing gate cases stayed green (`Tests 1 failed | 7 passed | 3 skipped (11)`).
  - Restore: blob == HEAD `8d8ebfc14096`, and `git diff HEAD` was empty.
  - No dist step was needed. The tested gate is reached through relative `src` imports: the test, then `../commands/migrate/apply.js`, then `../../utils/organization-ownership-drop-gate.js`.
- **Typecheck**: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck` exited 0. `tsconfig.json` includes `src`, where the pin lives, and `check:test-typecheck` answered OK.
- **Unit tier**: `--project unit` gave 290 files passed. Two files answered PREREQUISITE ("packages/cli is not built"); after the CLI was built they passed, 29 tests. In total, 292 of 292 files and 4325 passed + 29 skipped.
- **Integration tier**: only the two files above ran locally. The rest of the tier is declared to CI.

## Gates

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 64 commands at `9b3d9d8daf`. On that head, in one pass over the built workspace, all 64 exited 0. Exit codes were captured before any pipe.
  - An earlier pass on `cf15feedf4`, before the changeset commit, was missing the workspace build. There, four commands (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:i18n`, `check:i18n-coverage`, `check:i18n-walk-parity`) exited 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET. That is not a measurement, and it was superseded by the pass above.
- `--ran` on `9b3d9d8daf`: `64 derived, 64 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`.
- `pnpm lint` (`eslint . --no-inline-config`) on `9b3d9d8daf`: exit 0, no output.
  - Control: the same eslint with `--format json` over the two changed `.ts` files linted 2 files, with 0 errors and 0 warnings.
- CI on this PR is not read here. Its check-runs are the record for every family CI runs.

## Acceptance notes

- **Docs (not edited; outside this card's file surface).** `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` (`:1000`-`:1006`) says "`organization_id` on any table the organization-ownership ceremony covers waits for a verified … run. These tables are the ADR-0131 D7 tables and the `sys_metadata` family." The first sentence is still exact. The second names the platform's set and not, for example, an application object that opts out of the column.
- **The pending changeset `.changeset/23429-v18-boot-refusal.md` (not edited; outside this card's file surface).** It describes this gate as refusing "any table in the ceremony's inventory". It also says "Only an `os migrate apply --allow-destructive` run that would drop an inventory table's `organization_id` is refused". Both changesets compile into the same release, and this one's FROM/TO supersedes those two sentences. They are reported for the seat to amend before release.
- **The refusal sentence in `apply.ts` (`:515`)** reads "…, which the organization-ownership ceremony owns that drop, and it has not verified …". That is a grammar slip in an existing runtime string, reused unchanged as the ruling asked. Carrier: none.
